title: Adding `else` and `elif`: Multiple Branches 🌿
description: Handle multiple scenarios elegantly with else and elif, the traffic cops of your code.

slides.title: Beyond Yes/No
slides.content:
# Real Hacking Has Many Outcomes

A port scan can find a port: open, closed, filtered. A login can be: success, wrong password, account locked. Use `else` and `elif` (else‑if) to define multiple branches.

slides.title: The if‑else Duo

quizData.question: You can have an `else` without an `if`.

slides.title: `elif` – Checking Another Condition
slides.content:
# Short for "else if"

When you need more than two paths, chain `elif`:
```python
response_code = 200
if response_code == 200:
    print("OK")
elif response_code == 404:
    print("Not Found")
elif response_code == 500:
    print("Server Error")
else:
    print("Unknown code")
```
It checks conditions in order, first match wins.

slides.title: elif in Action
slides.content: Classify a port by its number:

quizData.question: What will `x=10; if x>5: print('A'); elif x>8: print('B')` output?
quizData.explanation: The first true condition (x>5) runs; `elif` is skipped.

slides.title: The else is Optional
slides.content:
# You Can End with elif Too

```python
if threat_level == "critical":
    print("Evacuate!")
elif threat_level == "high":
    print("Alert security")
# if neither, do nothing
```
But it's often safer to have a final `else` to catch unexpected cases – like a default in a switch statement.

slides.title: Login Simulation
slides.content: A realistic login check with multiple outcomes:

quizData.question: If `attempt_u = "root"` and `user = "admin"`, what is printed?
quizData.explanation: The first condition `attempt_u != user` is true, so that block runs.

slides.title: Avoid Overlapping Conditions
slides.content:
# Order Matters for Efficiency

Put the most specific or most common condition first. If you have broad catches, place them later.
```python
# Bad
if port > 0:
    print("valid")
elif port == 80:
    print("HTTP")  # never reached
```
Always structure logically.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `if/elif` Instead of Many `if`s

When only one branch should run, use `elif`. Separate `if` statements are independent and could all execute, which may not be what you want.
